subject: W4-B Task 1 cancellation completion and booked inventory release boundary trace
evidenceLevel: source code analysis and disposable PostgreSQL schema trace

redResult.case: current accepted lifecycle model cannot represent or produce a completed CANCELLED canonical transition
redResult.scope: disposable PostgreSQL with migrations 001-006, 036, 041, 049-055. Proves that W4-A supports CANCELLATION_REQUESTED with zero inventory consequence; direct UPDATE on canonical_reservations or canonical_reservation_nights is rejected by immutability triggers; direct INSERT of CANCELLED event is rejected by check constraint; restricted worker has zero raw DML privileges on inventory_days or canonical_reservation_events; and zero cancellation completion or inventory release execution authorities exist in PostgreSQL.

firstFailingBoundary: Current canonical reservations can durably record CANCELLATION_REQUESTED but have no authorized mechanism to complete cancellation and release the exact booked allocation.

w4aCurrentLifecycle.allocationState: canonical_reservations.status = 'INVENTORY_COMMITTED' remains immutable W3 allocation truth.
w4aCurrentLifecycle.eventLedger: canonical_reservation_events append-only table strictly constrained to event_type IN ('CANCELLATION_REQUESTED').
w4aCurrentLifecycle.commandLedger: canonical_reservation_lifecycle_commands strictly constrained to command_type IN ('REQUEST_CANCELLATION').
w4aCurrentLifecycle.authorizationLedger: canonical_reservation_lifecycle_authorizations unforgeable command-bound capabilities issued by encho_lifecycle_issuer.
w4aCurrentLifecycle.workerContainment: encho_lifecycle_worker only consumes verified authorizations and cannot issue capabilities or directly mutate tables.
w4aCurrentLifecycle.inventoryConsequence: Zero inventory consequence: booked_units remains 1 and held_units remains 0 upon CANCELLATION_REQUESTED.

currentInventoryAllocationModel.finalizationMechanism: 052_canonical_reservation_hold_finalization.sql atomically increments inventory_days.booked_units (+night.units) and decrements held_units (-night.units) per stay night.
currentInventoryAllocationModel.allocationTruth: canonical_reservation_nights holds immutable (reservation_id, inventory_day_id, stay_date, units). Protected by ON DELETE RESTRICT foreign keys and canonical_reservation_nights_immutable trigger.
currentInventoryAllocationModel.quantityModel: The allocation schema is unit-aware, while the currently accepted Encho Direct booking path commits one unit per reservation-night.
currentInventoryAllocationModel.underflowInvariants: inventory_days enforces chk_inventory_days_booked_positive (booked_units >= 0) and chk_inventory_days_capacity (held_units + booked_units + blocked_units <= total_units).
currentInventoryAllocationModel.capacityDriftSafety: Decreasing booked_units reduces total utilized capacity, therefore inventory release can never violate chk_inventory_days_capacity even if total_units changed after booking.

existingInventoryDecrementPaths.LEGACY_CONTAINED: server.ts:16165 (PUT /api/user/bookings/:id/cancel) updates legacy bookings table status='cancelled'. Has zero foreign keys or connection to canonical_reservations or inventory_days.
existingInventoryDecrementPaths.TEST_ONLY: Direct SQL queries in tests (cr1_offer_authority.test.ts, destination_pools.test.ts, safety_observation.test.ts, workflow_engine.test.ts) mutate inventory_days.booked_units without canonical authority.
existingInventoryDecrementPaths.MISSING: Zero canonical functions or procedures exist across PostgreSQL or application services that decrement booked_units.

cancellationDecisionVsExecution.cancellationDecisionAuthority: MISSING as business/policy authority. No policy engine, Guest cancellation eligibility rules, Host approval logic, or automatic cancellation rules exist in the repository. W4-B implementation may create only an INTERNAL command-bound decision authority primitive. The executor must never invent the decision it executes.
cancellationDecisionVsExecution.cancellationExecutionAuthority: MISSING. Atomic execution authority ('given an authorized cancellation decision, atomically record CANCELLED and release booked inventory') is absent.
cancellationDecisionVsExecution.separationPrinciple: W4-B owns execution authority and must not hardcode commercial policy (e.g. days before check-in, refund percentage, host penalty tiers). W4-B accepts an unforgeable decision capability and executes the atomic lifecycle state change and inventory release.

proposedW4BConsequenceModel.flow: CANCELLATION DECISION AUTHORITY -> restricted cancellation executor -> atomic transaction: CANCELLED lifecycle event + completion command receipt + cancellation-specific full-release fence + per-night release evidence + exact booked_units decrements + decision capability consumption. All or none. (Do not implement in Task 1).
proposedW4BConsequenceModel.initialStateTransition: CANCELLATION_REQUESTED -> CANCELLED for the initial Encho Direct implementation proposal. Direct ACTIVE -> CANCELLED is not proposed for the current Encho Direct flow, leaving future architectural room for authoritative external-provider cancellation evidence that may not originate from an Encho CANCELLATION_REQUESTED event.
proposedW4BConsequenceModel.decisionAuthorizationCapability: canonical_reservation_cancellation_authorizations (or extended lifecycle authorizations) recording immutable decision approval with actor, origin, reason, and expiry.
proposedW4BConsequenceModel.completedLifecycleEvent: Append-only CANCELLED event in canonical_reservation_events with actor_kind, actor_principal, origin_kind, reason_code, and decision_authorization_id.
proposedW4BConsequenceModel.cancellationReleaseFence: canonical_reservation_cancellation_inventory_releases table with UNIQUE(reservation_id), ensuring one completed full cancellation produces exactly one full cancellation release consequence per reservation. This does not establish that a reservation may only ever have one inventory release of any kind, preserving a clean boundary for future W4-C modification/reallocation consequences.
proposedW4BConsequenceModel.perNightReleaseEvidence: REQUIRED. Proposed W4-B contract must include per-night release evidence conceptually equivalent to canonical_reservation_cancellation_release_nights bound to: cancellation release ID, reservation ID, canonical reservation-night identity, inventory_day_id, stay_date, and released_units. The release executor must derive these values exclusively from immutable canonical_reservation_nights, never from caller-supplied parameters.
proposedW4BConsequenceModel.underflowAndAtomicityContract: For every canonical_reservation_night, the corresponding inventory_day row must exist and inventory_days.booked_units >= reservation_night.units before decrement. If any allocation cannot be reconciled, the entire cancellation execution transaction rolls back. No clamp-to-zero, no partial release, no partial CANCELLED event, and no partial per-night evidence.
proposedW4BConsequenceModel.atomicExecutionProcedure: canonical_complete_reservation_cancellation PL/pgSQL function executing event append, command receipt, cancellation release fence, per-night release evidence, and inventory decrements in a single transaction.
proposedW4BConsequenceModel.lockOrdering: Design candidate: reservation -> cancellation decision authorization -> command/consequence authority -> inventory_days in deterministic ordering. The proposed ordering is compatible with the inspected W4-A model and must be validated against W3 and inventory/calendar writers during W4-B implementation.
proposedW4BConsequenceModel.replayModel: Durable command receipts and cancellation release fence ensure replayed commands return the committed completion result without double-decrementing inventory.

deferredBoundaries.publicGuestApi: Deferred until session ingress and policy engines are mounted.

refundSeparation.principle: Cancellation completion and inventory release are independent of whatever future refund/money outcome authority determines.
refundSeparation.status: Refund authority does not exist yet. W4-B does not compute refund entitlement, does not create refund state, does not call payment providers, and does not rewrite payment capture truth. W4-D will define the canonical money/refund model later.

externalChannelCompatibility.qualification: A future external-channel cancellation can use the same mechanical cancellation executor only if the external reservation ingestion path has already recorded equivalent canonical inventory allocation truth sufficient for release, such as canonical reservation-night allocations and corresponding booked inventory. Current W4-B Task 1 does not prove that external-channel ingestion currently creates such allocation truth. No STAAH compatibility certification claim is made.

conclusion: Current canonical reservations can durably record CANCELLATION_REQUESTED but have no authorized mechanism to complete cancellation and release the exact booked allocation. The allocation schema is unit-aware, while the currently accepted Encho Direct booking path commits one unit per reservation-night. The proposed W4-B consequence model establishes an atomic execution transaction consisting of: CANCELLED event append, completion command receipt, cancellation-specific full-release fence (canonical_reservation_cancellation_inventory_releases), required per-night release evidence (canonical_reservation_cancellation_release_nights derived exclusively from canonical_reservation_nights), exact booked_units decrements with underflow verification, and decision capability consumption. Cancellation execution remains strictly separate from absent business/policy decision authorities and unbuilt W4-D refund models.
limitations: No runtime implementation, no migration 056, no money movement, no external APIs contacted. This is intentional red diagnostic and trace evidence for W4-B Task 1.
